solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Working during month near start of year in UK?

indicators.note: near says the first letter of year sits beside the month built so far
during puts the word for working inside the month's name

parts.note: March is a month
a machine that is working is on

indicators.note: start of takes only the opening letter of year

explanation.surface: A question about some job being done in the UK one month, near New Year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working' looks like the subject, but it is ON, placed in MARCH; the question mark flags that the UK is only an example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The United Kingdom is an example of a state with a king or queen as head.

clue.text: How GP might refer to successful case with treated hand?

definitions.text: How GP might refer to successful case
definitions.meaning: a family doctor boasting of a patient made well might say this, read as three words
having had the hands and nails professionally tended

explanation.surface: A doctor's success story about a patient whose hand got better.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as MAN I CURED: what a GP (family doctor) might say of a recovered patient.
explanation.definitionFit: Groomed nails and hands are the result of a beauty treatment for the hands.

clue.text: Actor/director entertains Sun journalist

indicators.note: entertains means takes in as a guest, so the star holds the letter inside

parts.note: Paul Newman was a film actor who also directed
S is the abbreviation for Sun, as in Sunday

explanation.surface: A Hollywood figure hosts a reporter from The Sun newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sun' looks like the British tabloid but is just S.
explanation.definitionFit: A reporter gathering and writing news is a journalist.

clue.text: Approaching the age of rebellion

definitions.meaning: a child ... five is about to reach that age

explanation.definitionFit: The word means nearing an age and also a revolt such as the Easter uprising.

clue.text: You foolishly got on horse with name twice held by the Queen's horse

indicators.note: held by puts all the rest inside the royal initials

parts.note: HM is Her Majesty

indicators.note: got on means mounted beside, so the pair follows the shuffled letters
foolishly means the letters of you are jumbled
twice says the pair of letters appears two times

parts.note: horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

explanation.surface: You foolishly mounted a horse belonging to the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'horse' is H (heroin); the second is the definition. Swift's Gulliver's Travels names the rational horses.
explanation.definitionFit: In Gulliver's Travels, Swift's wise talking horses are given this name.

clue.text: Sweet child taking second university course ahead of time

indicators.note: ahead of says the course comes before the time letter

parts.note: a mo is a brief moment, a second
PPE is Philosophy, Politics and Economics, an Oxford degree

explanation.surface: A child prodigy who starts a second university degree early.
explanation.walkthrough: PPE (Philosophy, Politics and Economics) is a well-known British university course.
explanation.definitionFit: A moppet is an affectionate word for a small, endearing youngster.

clue.text: Sentimental single initially released by US band — covered by Wham, surprisingly

indicators.note: covered by means wrapped inside the shuffled letters
surprisingly signals that the letters of Wham turn up in an unexpected order
released by means let go from the band, so that letter drops out

parts.note: Kiss is an American rock band

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of single

explanation.surface: A sappy single from an American group, covered by Wham! to everyone's surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: Kiss is a US rock band; 'single' is not a record here but just supplies its first letter, which the band lets go.
explanation.definitionFit: Mawkish means sickly or excessively sentimental.

clue.text: A long lost former college, previously having properties found in a square

definitions.text: having properties found in a square

indicators.note: previously places the college before the remaining letters

parts.note: a poly was a British polytechnic, a college type since abolished

indicators.note: lost here means confused, so the letters of a long are mixed up

explanation.surface: A once-familiar college, long gone, used to own property in a town square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' rearranges A LONG into GONAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A square is a many-sided plane figure, so it has the features of such shapes.

clue.text: Finding Lee Evans a little pointless becomes awful bind

indicators.note: becomes awful signals the remaining letters are mangled into a new order
a little pointless means short of one point, so one compass letter E is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone finds comedian Lee Evans slightly pointless, a dreadful chore.
explanation.walkthrough: Lee Evans is a British comedian. LEEEVANS loses one E (a point, east), and 'becomes awful' rearranges the LEEVANS that remains.
explanation.definitionFit: To enslave is to bind someone in servitude.

clue.text: State some answers in full

parts.note: the consonants N, S and W in the word answers are the abbreviation of an Australian state; spelling that abbreviation out in full gives its name

explanation.surface: An instruction to give some of your answers completely rather than abbreviated.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters NSW sit inside 'answers', and NSW is the standard abbreviation for an Australian state; writing it 'in full' gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue names an Australian state whose capital is Sydney, by expanding its familiar initials.

clue.text: See 8
American Indian from Taco? Manchester, apparently

indicators.note: from says the letters are drawn out of the words that follow, across the gap

explanation.surface: Someone guesses where a taco comes from: Manchester, it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: The Comanche are a Native American people of the southern Great Plains.

clue.text: Gloomy Dean meets Arab, dressed and ready to go

parts.note: William Inge, Dean of St Paul's, was nicknamed the Gloomy Dean
Ar. is a standard abbreviation for Arab or Arabic

explanation.surface: A miserable clergyman meets an Arab, both dressed and about to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: Dean W. R. Inge of St Paul's Cathedral, London, was known as 'the Gloomy Dean' for his pessimistic sermons.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in gear is both to be kitted out and, like an engaged car, ready to move off.

clue.text: Use a variety of approaches, making hen grit?

parts.note: the letters of hen grit are those of ... the reshuffled, so this is what you get by making changes to ... the

explanation.surface: A farmer trying many methods ends up feeding a hen grit.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: rearrange the letters of RING THE and HEN GRIT results. The question mark flags this reverse working.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring the changes is an idiom from bell-ringing meaning to vary how something is done.

clue.text: Blow, that's hard, keeping 11 without a drink

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the reduced answer goes within the gale

parts.note: a gale is a hard blow of wind

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the letter a comes out of it

parts.note: 11 refers to the answer to 11 across

explanation.surface: A hard blow, and someone stays thirsty without a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: '11' is a cross-reference: it stands for the answer to 11 across, which 'without a' then trims.
explanation.definitionFit: A fizzy ginger-flavoured soft drink, often used as a mixer.

clue.text: See 12
Go in after fish and chips

definitions.note: the nickname for one woodworker, though plural in form

indicators.note: after places entering behind the fish

parts.note: a carp is a fish
to go in is to enter

explanation.surface: Go in for some fish and chips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fish and chips' reads as a British takeaway, but 'Chips' is the traditional nickname for a ship's woodworker.
explanation.definitionFit: Chips or chippy is British slang for a woodworker who builds and repairs wooden things.

clue.text: Swiftly and suddenly remove little old man in authority

indicators.note: in places the small father within the power

parts.note: to hold sway is to have authority
wee is Scottish for little
pa is a father, one's old man

explanation.surface: Someone wants a small elderly official abruptly removed from power.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear something off fast and completely, as a flood does houses.

clue.text: A place to walk when depressed, with note nearly composed

parts.note: feeling depressed is feeling down
a memo is a short written note

indicators.note: composed means put together, so the letters of nearly are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A walk to take when feeling low, with a song almost finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' looks like 'calm' or 'written', but it rearranges NEARLY into RYLANE.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a figurative path one strolls along when reminiscing about the past.

clue.text: Visibly performing number about men only

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the number goes round the men-only word

parts.note: one is a number
a stag party or night is for men only

explanation.surface: A performer sings a number about a men-only gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: A stag party is a British pre-wedding night out for men.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer in view of the audience is out there in the spotlight.

clue.text: Vessels in river area

indicators.note: in places the vessels within the river

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
pans are cooking vessels

explanation.surface: Boats out on a stretch of river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessels' suggests boats, but here they are cooking pans. The Exe is a river in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: An expanse is a wide, open area, such as of sea or land.

clue.text: See 17
In A&E, a role involved nipple rings

indicators.note: In says the shuffled words go within the hospital letters

parts.note: A&E is a hospital's accident and emergency department, written AE

indicators.note: involved means tangled, so the letters of a role are mixed

explanation.surface: A casualty department worker's job involved dealing with body piercings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges A ROLE into REOLA.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the pigmented circles of skin around the nipples.

clue.text: Spent summer in France just south of its capital, we hear

indicators.note: just south of means beneath, and in a down answer the summer word sits under the spoken letter
we hear means the letter is written as it is spoken

parts.note: the capital letter of France is F
ete is French for summer

explanation.surface: A summer holiday in France, just south of Paris, has been used up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like Paris, but it is France's capital letter, F, spoken as EFF, with ETE below.
explanation.definitionFit: Effete means exhausted or worn out, having lost its vigour.

clue.text: A PM's turned out

indicators.note: turned says the word is flipped to read the other way

parts.note: Robert Peel was a British Prime Minister, so the PM's gives Peel's

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister has been ejected from office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned out' reads as one phrase meaning ousted, but 'turned' reverses PEELS and 'out' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sleeping is said to be out, as in out cold or out like a light.

clue.text: Keep quiet about fairy on front of rock band's Book of Smiles?

indicators.note: on front of places the wrapped fairy before the band
about means surrounding, so the hush goes round the fairy

parts.note: sh is the command to keep quiet
an elf is a fairy creature
ELP is Emerson, Lake and Palmer, a rock band

explanation.surface: A rock band is told to keep the fairy quiet on its jolly songbook cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smiles' is not grinning but Samuel Smiles, Victorian author of the 1859 book of this title.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Smiles wrote the famous Victorian guide to personal improvement by one's own effort.

clue.text: Wealth produced going after profit in a way that's criminal

indicators.note: going after says the shuffled wealth follows the rest
in places the profit within the letters for a way

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
a profit is a gain

indicators.note: produced means made into something new, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Riches made by chasing profit in some illegal manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produced' rearranges WEALTH into THELAW.
explanation.definitionFit: An act that breaks legal rules is criminal; the phrase is a common synonym.

clue.text: See 25
Hard cut to point

parts.note: to sever is to cut off
E is a compass point, east

explanation.surface: An instruction to cut something hard so it comes to a point, like whittling.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard and severe are synonyms for harsh or strict, as in a hard winter.

clue.text: Writer with tips for really decorative stuff that needs to be cut

definitions.text: decorative stuff that needs to be cut

parts.note: Graham Greene was an English novelist

indicators.note: tips for takes the two end letters of really

explanation.surface: An author gives handy pointers about ornamental things that must be trimmed.
explanation.definitionFit: Foliage used as decoration, such as hedging or cut leaves, has to be trimmed.
